facts.raw_span: 4 months of progressively worsening symmetric pain in the small joints of her hands, wrists, knees, and ankles
early morning stiffness lasting 2 hours daily
severe fatigue throughout the day
mild COVID-19 infection confirmed by SARS-CoV-2 PCR
denied fever, chills, night sweats, weight loss, rash, or appetite changes since recovering
erythrocyte sedimentation rate of 13 mm/hour
C-reactive protein of 4.3 mg/L
antinuclear antibody titer of 1:640
rheumatoid factor of 62.29 IU/mL
anti-cyclic citrullinated peptide antibody of 237.39 units
MRI of the hands demonstrated synovitis of the bilateral distal radioulnar joints and the left second metacarpophalangeal joint
tenosynovitis around the extensor carpi ulnaris tendon

concepts.why: The patient presents with symmetric pain in the small joints, early morning stiffness, and severe fatigue, which are classic symptoms of rheumatoid arthritis, and is supported by the presence of rheumatoid factor and anti-cyclic citrullinated peptide antibody.

Although the patient has a positive rheumatoid factor, the presence of synovitis and tenosynovitis on MRI suggests an inflammatory arthritis, and seronegative rheumatoid arthritis is a possible diagnosis.
The patient's recent history of COVID-19 infection and the presence of symmetric pain in the small joints and tenosynovitis on MRI suggest a possible diagnosis of reactive arthritis.
Although there is no mention of psoriasis, the presence of synovitis and tenosynovitis on MRI and the patient's symptoms suggest a possible diagnosis of psoriatic arthritis.
The patient's symptoms of fatigue, joint pain, and the presence of an antinuclear antibody titer suggest a possible diagnosis of systemic lupus erythematosus.
The patient's symptoms and laboratory results do not fit a specific connective tissue disease, but rather suggest an undifferentiated connective tissue disease.
The patient's symptoms and laboratory results suggest an inflammatory arthritis, although the specific type is unclear.
The patient's recent history of COVID-19 infection and the presence of symmetric pain in the small joints suggest a possible diagnosis of post-infectious arthritis.

rationales.F01: Symmetric small joint pain is a hallmark of Rheumatoid Arthritis.
rationales.F02: Early morning stiffness is a common symptom of Rheumatoid Arthritis and other inflammatory arthritides.
rationales.F04: Recent infection can trigger Reactive Arthritis or Post-infectious Arthritis.
rationales.F08: High antinuclear antibody titers can be seen in Systemic Lupus Erythematosus and other autoimmune diseases.
rationales.F09: Elevated rheumatoid factor is a specific marker for Rheumatoid Arthritis.
rationales.F10: Presence of anti-cyclic citrullinated peptide antibodies is highly specific for Rheumatoid Arthritis.
rationales.F11: Synovitis on MRI is a characteristic feature of Rheumatoid Arthritis and other inflammatory arthritides.

frontier_selector.rationale: The patient's symptoms of symmetric pain in small joints, early morning stiffness, and elevated rheumatoid factor and anti-cyclic citrullinated peptide antibody levels strongly support Rheumatoid Arthritis, with no unexplained strong contradictions.
